title: Computers
subtitle: hardware, software, back up, upgrade, crash
summary: Name the parts of a computer and the programs you run on it, and use the verbs that go with them.

lesson.heading: Hardware: the equipment itself
rows: personal computer / PC / desktop computer
a computer that fits on a desk, used by individuals at work or at home
laptop (computer)
a lightweight portable computer that usually fits in a briefcase
tablet
a portable personal computer operated by a touch screen
hard disk
a device inside a computer that stores large amounts of information
disk drive
a device that allows information to be read from a disk
scanner
a device for transferring pictures and texts into a computer
memory stick
a small device that lets you carry data anywhere and plug it into any machine
lesson.note: **Hardware** is computer equipment or machinery; a **device** is a piece of equipment.

lesson.heading: Inside the machine
rows: RAM (random access memory)
the memory available on a computer to store and use information temporarily, measured in gigabytes
(micro)chip
a very small piece of semiconductor containing extremely small electronic circuits, which can perform particular operations
network
a number of computers connected together (or networked) so that they can share information

lesson.heading: Software: the programs you install
lesson.text: An **application** is a piece of software designed for a specific purpose; this is often shortened to **app**. **Word-processing** means writing and storing printed text on a computer, and a **spreadsheet** is a program - or the grid you create with it - for mathematical operations.

examples.text: You can get mobile phone **apps** for all sorts of things these days.
**Word-processing** programs make it very easy to write text and to format it.
I keep the household accounts on a **spreadsheet**.

lesson.heading: More software words
rows: database
a large amount of information stored so that it can easily be looked at or changed
(computer) graphics
pictures, images and symbols that you can form on a computer
virus
hidden instructions in a program designed to destroy information
display
what you see on the screen of an electronic device
icon
a small symbol on the display that opens a program
cursor
the mark that shows where you are on the screen
lesson.note: You put the **cursor** on the **icon** you want to use and **click on** it to open it.

lesson.heading: Storing and losing your work
lesson.text: You **store** a lot of important information on your computer, so it is sensible to **back up** all your files on a regular basis. Then it is less of a problem if you **delete** something accidentally or if your computer **crashes**.

examples.text: I **back up** my files on a memory stick every Friday.
My laptop **crashed** and I lost a whole morning's work.

lesson.heading: Correcting and improving
lesson.text: Most applications let you **undo** what you have just done, so it is quick and easy to correct anything you have **keyed in** by mistake. After a few years you may want to **upgrade** your computer so that you can still **run** all the software you need; you can usually **download** upgrades from company websites.

examples.text: Just click on Undo to **undo** the last change.
It's easy to correct anything you have **keyed in** by mistake.
They are always developing machines which are faster and more powerful, so you may want to **upgrade**.
If you don't do this you may not be able to **run** all the software you need.
You can **download** upgrades to your operating system from company websites.

lesson.text: *Back up* is a verb (back up your files) and *backup* is a noun (keep a backup). The same goes for *upgrade* and *download*.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of hardware with its description.

pairs.right: transfers pictures and texts into a computer
a small device for carrying data from machine to machine
stores large amounts of information inside the computer
a lightweight portable computer that fits in a briefcase
a portable computer operated by a touch screen
computers connected so that they can share information

exercises.prompt: I've lost a lot of data. I wonder if my computer has a ___.
exercises.explanation: A virus is hidden instructions in a program designed to destroy information.

exercises.prompt: A lot of people carry their ___ on aeroplanes and work on them during the flight.
exercises.explanation: A laptop is a lightweight portable computer.

exercises.prompt: I've got such a lot of photos, music and videos stored on my computer that my ___ is almost full.
exercises.hint: (two words - it stores information inside the machine)
exercises.explanation: The hard disk is the device inside a computer that stores large amounts of information.

exercises.prompt: That computer game you gave me has got amazing ___ - the people just look so realistic!
exercises.explanation: Computer graphics are the pictures, images and symbols formed on a computer.

exercises.prompt: One of my most important tasks at work is to keep the ___ up to date so that customers' contact details are always accurate.
exercises.hint: (one word - stored information you can look at or change)
exercises.explanation: A database stores information so that it can easily be looked at or changed.

exercises.prompt: If you put the ___ in the middle of a paragraph of text and double click, you select the whole paragraph.
exercises.explanation: The cursor shows where you are on the screen.

exercises.prompt: I downloaded a fantastic ___ the other day - it tells me where the nearest cash machine is.
exercises.explanation: An app (application) is a piece of software designed for a specific purpose.

exercises.prompt: If you don't want to lose computer data, what must you do?
exercises.explanation: You back up your files so you still have them if the computer crashes.

exercises.prompt: If you accidentally delete some text you've just been working on, what can you do?
options: Undo what you have just done.
exercises.explanation: Undo reverses what you have just done.

exercises.prompt: If your computer is old and working very slowly, what might you consider doing?
exercises.explanation: You upgrade an old computer so that it can run newer software.

exercises.prompt: Is each item hardware or software?

exercises.statement: If you buy new software when you have an old operating system, you may find that the new software won't run.
exercises.explanation: Correct. That is why people upgrade: an old machine may not run the software you need.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to give some sensible advice.
exercises.answer: It's sensible to back up all your files on a regular basis.
exercises.explanation: Back up your files so you don't lose them if the computer crashes.
